title: Aliased Mutable Pointer Coupling (Shared Mutable State)
pattern: Two distinct application modules or threads hold a shared, cloneable reference to mutable heap state, mutating it concurrently.
why_bad: It couples the components across time. If the relative timing of mutations changes, the application experiences non-deterministic race conditions. Understanding the logic requires tracing the entire history of both components.
detection: The propagation of cloned `Arc<Mutex<T>>` or `Rc<RefCell<T>>` structures to multiple independent structs that run distinct workflows.
counterexample: Explicit lock-free concurrent data structures or synchronized channels designed specifically for concurrent message passing.
source: Eric Elliott, *Composing Software* (2019) ("Mutable State Dependencies"); Martin Kleppmann, *Designing Data-Intensive Applications* (2017), Chapter 9 ("Ordering Guarantees").
